properties.description:
Four tests over the real `ReflowService`, driving the tool methods a client calls rather than the engine beneath them.

**The claim:** a read-only service REFUSES a write (`create_node`).

**Three counterweights, and each catches a different way the fix could go wrong:**
- `a_read_only_service_still_serves_reads` — a read-only surface that refused reads too would be no surface at all, and reading is the entire thing being offered.
- `a_normal_service_still_writes` — catches the fix going too far. It asserts a DEFAULT service reports `is_read_only() == false` and writes successfully, so it goes red if read-only ever becomes a default or if `write_lock` starts refusing unconditionally. **It passed BEFORE the refusal existed and after**, which is what makes it a counterweight rather than a restatement.
- `a_session_on_a_read_only_server_is_read_only_too` — ⭐ the case the COMPILER found, not review. `share()` mints a service per CLIENT SESSION (`req:sessions-share-a-graph`), and that is the path every connection to a shared server takes. Had read-only been reset there instead of inherited, the mode would have held for the process and evaporated for every actual client — read-only in name only, and green at the process level.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHECK: that reads are SAFE to expose. It checks integrity, not confidentiality. A read-only surface still hands the whole design to anyone who can reach the port, which the requirement relocates to the network rather than solving.
properties.findings:
2026-10-02: 5 of 5 pass, including the new a_read_only_service_writes_no_file_a_tool_is_asked_to_write: a read-only server and a session it mints refuse export_graph and export_surface with a path and leave no file, export into the reply still answers, and an ordinary service and a snapshot copy still write the file (chg:every-one-shot-mode-resolves-its-design-first-and-every-flag-is-honoured-or-refused-2026-10-02).

EARLIER RUN (2026-08-26), kept: 4 passed / 0 failed. ⭐ OBSERVED FAILING FIRST: run against the plumbing with the refusal deliberately absent, the two write cases went red (`a_read_only_service_refuses_a_write`, `a_session_on_a_read_only_server_is_read_only_too`) while both counterweights were green — which is what proves the counterweights are not restatements of the fix. Full workspace suite after: 1817 passed / 0 failed across 159 binaries, run whole rather than the core-only gate because 98 call sites moved. `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -p reflow2-mcp -D warnings` clean.

📌 DEMONSTRATED IN THE FIELD, not only in tests: the shared server serving this session was stopped and respawned from the newly-built binary (read-only compiled in, flag absent) and design writes continued normally — including the ChangeEvent recording this work. That is the check a user actually wants for a change of this shape, and it is not something the test suite can make.
properties.name: A read-only surface refuses writes, still serves reads, and a client session inherits the mode
